reply_text:
Using last fetch on the Seoul keynote report.I found eight dated statements from 2025. Three are new and come from transcripts or printed interviews I opened. One more is new but I only saw it in news coverage. Two match claims you already have. The last two come from a moderator's write-up, where LeCun's answers are mostly paraphrased.

**New, his own words on the page:**
- **Six Five "View from Davos" interview (January 2025, WEF).** Over the next two years, progress will come from LLMs with extra parts "bolted on". Also: "perhaps in five years we'll know if we're on the good path towards something like human level intelligence." The exact day isn't on the page. The video sits with Six Five's WEF25 coverage, around 21–23 January.
- **AI Inside podcast (recorded 4 April, published 9 April).** If Meta's research succeeds, "maybe within ten years, we'll have a good handle on whether we can reach that goal" of human-level intelligence. The line just before it is the claim you already have. You may want to fold this one into that file.

**Same claim as your files:**
- In the same Davos interview he says early progress on the new paradigm will come "within three to five years". That matches your 2025-01-23 file, though your file probably comes from a different Davos session.
- The AI Inside lines "not going to happen next year… two years from now… may happen… within the next ten years" match your 2025-04-09 file.

**Weaker sources:**
- **MIT symposium (October 2025), news coverage only.** "Within three to five years" world models, not LLMs, will be the dominant AI architecture. I read it on Axios, which was itself relying on a Wall Street Journal profile. It closely repeats your January "LLMs not central within five years" claim, but at a later event, so I left it as a new entry.
- **CES fireside chat (January 2025), moderator's write-up.** The moderator put two true/false statements to him. "An AI agent will have research accepted at a conference such as NeurIPS within five years": he answered "False", and "False" again for ten years. Those one-word answers are his only quoted words. The other statement was that a "ChatGPT moment" for robotics is around the corner. His own reply was a joke; the claim that he expected it "within 3-5 years" is the moderator's paraphrase. Treat both as weak.

**Not used:**
- The October Seoul keynote ("LLMs will be obsolete within 5 years") is a likely missing claim. The article's page refused to open, so I quote nothing from it. It is the obvious next page to open by hand.
- An article summarising a Financial Times interview gives a timeline ("baby versions within 12 months", animal-level AI in five to seven years). It is all the article's paraphrase, and I couldn't confirm when the interview took place, so I left it out.
- I ran 11 of 12 searches and used all 6 page openings, one of which failed.
